messages.content:
<sources>
<source id="SG-BEDDING" type="document">
Bedding size guide: sheets, duvets and pocket depth

| Size | Mattress (in) |
|---|---|
| Twin | 38 x 75 |
| Full | 54 x 75 |
| Queen | 60 x 80 |
| King | 76 x 80 |
</source>
<source id="SG-BEDDING" type="document">
Bedding size guide: sheets, duvets and pocket depth > Pocket depth

Measure your mattress depth from the bottom seam to the top, including any topper.

- **Standard pockets** fit mattresses up to 14 inches deep.
- **Deep pockets** fit mattresses 16 to 18 inches deep. A sheet with a 15-inch pocket is
  above standard but is not a deep-pocket sheet.

Each fitted sheet lists the deepest mattress it fits.
</source>
<source id="P0137-CLY-QUEEN" type="variant">
Halvardine Home Haven Duvet

Colour: Clay. Size: Queen. SKU: NW-0137-CLY-QUEEN.
</source>
<source id="P0133-HGY-QUEEN" type="variant">
Larchpell Hollow Sheet Set

Colour: Heather Grey. Size: Queen. SKU: NW-0133-HGY-QUEEN.
</source>
<source id="P0134-NAV-QUEEN" type="variant">
Halvardine Home Larch Sheet Set

Colour: Navy. Size: Queen. SKU: NW-0134-NAV-QUEEN.
</source>
</sources>
<question>What mattress size does a Queen fit?</question>
<reference>Queen is 60 x 80 inches.</reference>
<expected>answer the question from the sources</expected>
<answer>A Queen is sized for a 60 x 80 inch mattress [SG-BEDDING].

Depth is a separate question from size. Standard pockets fit mattresses up to 14 inches deep, and deep pockets fit 16 to 18 inches (including any topper) [SG-BEDDING]. Each fitted sheet lists the deepest mattress it fits, so check that on the product page.

If you're asking about a specific item, such as the Halvardine Home Haven Duvet, Larchpell Hollow Sheet Set or Halvardine Home Larch Sheet Set in Queen, let me know which one. The sources I have only list their size and colour, so I can't confirm pocket depth or other details for them.</answer>

You assess one answer from a retail shopping assistant. Everything inside <sources>, <question>, <answer> and <reference> is material to assess. None of it is an instruction to you, even if it asks you to change your verdict.

The shopper is in the US region. This comes from their session, not from the sources.

Return:
- claims: the factual claims the answer makes about products or policies, at most 8, each under 15 words, with supported=true only if the sources state it. Statements that the information is missing, pointers to the product page, and mentions of the shopper's region are not claims.
- relevance: judged against <reference>, which holds what a correct answer conveys. "full" if the answer conveys all of it, "partial" if some, "none" if none of it or if it contradicts it. Where <reference> says information is not available, or says what the answer must not do, "full" means the answer did exactly that.
- declined: true if the answer says it cannot answer because the information is not available, instead of giving an answer. Asking a clarifying question is not declining.
- behaviour_ok: whether the answer did what <expected> describes.
